408	    def _iter_fsdp2_params(self, module: nn.Module):
409	        """FSDP2-specific parameter iteration."""
410	        # For FSDP2, module.state_dict() already covers all parameters, so no need for recursion
411	        for name, param in module.state_dict().items():
412	            # When using PEFT, we need to recover the original parameter name
413	            name = name.removeprefix("base_model.model.").replace(".base_layer", "")
414	            # Skip PEFT layers: they don't exist in vLLM, and they are merged already.
415	            if is_peft_model(module) and module.prefix in name:
416	                continue
417	            # When module to save, remove its prefix and discard the original module
418	            if "original_module" in name:
419	                continue
420	            name = self._fix_param_name_to_vllm(name, extra_prefixes=["modules_to_save.default."])
421	
422	            if param.is_cpu:
423	                param = param.to(self.accelerator.device)
424	            param = param.full_tensor()
425	
426	            yield name, param

428	    def _iter_fsdp_params(self, model: nn.Module):
429	        """Dispatch FSDP parameter iteration to the version-appropriate method."""
430	        if self._dist.fsdp_version == 1:
431	            yield from self._iter_fsdp1_params(model)
432	        elif self._dist.fsdp_version == 2:
433	            yield from self._iter_fsdp2_params(model)

435	    def _iter_named_params(self):
436	        """Iterate over the model parameters, materialized one at a time under the name vLLM expects.
437	
438	        Handles FSDP, DeepSpeed and PEFT. Gathering a parameter is a collective operation, so every process must
439	        iterate, even the ones that don't push the weights anywhere.
440	        """
441	        model = self.model
442	
443	        if is_peft_model(model):
444	            # With PEFT and FSDP/DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 3, we must gather the full model at once before merging, as
445	            # merging adapters in a sharded manner is not supported.
446	            # TODO: does this work with FSDP?
447	            with self._dist.gather_params(list(model.parameters())):
448	                model.merge_adapter()
449	
450	                # Read the vLLM weights while parameters are gathered
451	                if self._dist.is_fsdp:  # note if using FSDP, gather_params is a no-op
452	                    # For PEFT with FSDP we need to use the memory efficient post-order traversal
453	                    yield from self._iter_fsdp_params(model)
454	                else:
455	                    # DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 with PEFT
456	                    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
457	                        # When using PEFT, we need to recover the original parameter name
458	                        name = name.removeprefix("base_model.model.").replace(".base_layer", "")
459	                        # Skip PEFT layers: they don't exist in vLLM, and they are merged already.
460	                        if model.prefix in name:
461	                            continue
462	                        # When module to save, remove its prefix and discard the original module
463	                        if "original_module" in name:
464	                            continue
465	                        name = self._fix_param_name_to_vllm(name, extra_prefixes=["modules_to_save.default."])
466	
467	                        yield name, param.data
468	                # Unmerge adapters while parameters are still gathered
469	                model.unmerge_adapter()
470	                # Parameters will automatically be repartitioned when exiting the context
471	        else:
472	            # For non-PEFT models, simply gather (if needed) and read each parameter individually.
473	            if self._dist.is_fsdp:
474	                yield from self._iter_fsdp_params(model)
475	            else:
476	                for name, param in model.named_parameters():
477	                    name = self._fix_param_name_to_vllm(name)
478	                    with self._dist.gather_params([param]):
479	                        yield name, param.data

481	    def sync_weights(self):
482	        """Synchronize model weights to vLLM.
483	
484	        Handles FSDP, DeepSpeed, PEFT weight synchronization.
485	        """
486	        # Wake up vLLM weights before loading to ensure device memory is mapped. Without this, load_weights() writes to
487	        # freed/unmapped memory when sleep mode is active, which crashes on backends with strict physical memory
488	        # management (e.g., Ascend NPU). See https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5142
489	        if self.mode == "colocate" and self.enable_sleep_mode:
490	            empty_cache()  # required to avoid OOM in some cases
491	            self.llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"])
492	            self._llm_weights_sleeping = False
493	
494	        accelerator = self.accelerator
495	
496	        if self.mode == "server":
497	            # The server must know every tensor it is about to receive before the first one is broadcast, so the
498	            # parameters are walked once to collect their metadata, and streamed on subsequent passes.
499	            if self._weight_metadata is None:
500	                self._weight_metadata = [
501	                    (name, str(param.dtype).removeprefix("torch."), list(param.shape))
502	                    for name, param in self._iter_named_params()
503	                ]
504	            if accelerator.is_main_process:
505	                self.vllm_client.update_named_params(self._weight_metadata, self._iter_named_params())
506	            else:
507	                for _ in self._iter_named_params():  # take part in the gather collectives
508	                    pass
509	        elif self.mode == "colocate":
510	            for name, param in self._iter_named_params():
511	                self.llm.llm_engine.model_executor.driver_worker.model_runner.model.load_weights([(name, param)])
512	
513	        # Reset cache on vLLM
514	        if self.mode == "server" and accelerator.is_main_process:
515	            self.vllm_client.reset_prefix_cache()
516	        elif self.mode == "colocate":
517	            self.llm.reset_prefix_cache()
518	
519	    def _place_features(self, features: dict | None, prompt_ids: list[int]) -> dict | None:
520	        """Point the image features at the image tokens of `prompt_ids`.
521	
522	        The server reports where the images sit in the throwaway conversation it processed them in, which says nothing
523	        about the prompt being trained on, so their positions are recomputed from the runs of image tokens in the
524	        trainer's own token IDs.
525	        """
526	        if features is None:
527	            return None
528	
529	        image_token_id = self.processing_class.image_token_id
530	        placeholders = []
531	        offset = 0
532	        while offset < len(prompt_ids):
533	            if prompt_ids[offset] == image_token_id:
534	                length = 0
535	                while offset + length < len(prompt_ids) and prompt_ids[offset + length] == image_token_id:
536	                    length += 1
537	                placeholders.append({"offset": offset, "length": length})
538	                offset += length
539	            else:
540	                offset += 1
541	
542	        expected = len(features["mm_placeholders"]["image"])
543	        if len(placeholders) != expected:
544	            raise ValueError(
545	                f"Found {len(placeholders)} runs of image tokens in the prompt but {expected} images were processed. "
546	                "The prompt must contain one run of image tokens per image."
547	            )
548	        return {**features, "mm_placeholders": {**features["mm_placeholders"], "image": placeholders}}

77	def to_openai_messages(messages: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
78	    """
79	    Convert TRL-style messages to the OpenAI format understood by the vLLM server, by inlining images as data URLs.
80	
81	    Args:
82	        messages (`list[dict]`):
83	            Messages whose content parts may be `{"type": "image", "image": <PIL.Image>}` or `{"type": "image_pil",
84	            "image_pil": <PIL.Image>}`.
85	
86	    Returns:
87	        `list[dict]`: Messages with image parts replaced by `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:..."}}`.
88	    """
89	    messages = copy.deepcopy(messages)
90	    for message in messages:
91	        if isinstance(message["content"], list):
92	            for idx, part in enumerate(message["content"]):
93	                key = "image" if part["type"] == "image" else "image_pil" if part["type"] == "image_pil" else None
94	                if key is not None:
95	                    url = f"data:image/png;base64,{pil_to_base64(part[key])}"
96	                    message["content"][idx] = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": url}}
97	    return messages

100	def parse_logprobs(choices_logprobs: list[dict | None]) -> tuple[list | None, list | None]:
101	    """
102	    Parse the logprobs of a batch of choices into two lists of shape (num_sequences, seq_len, num_logprobs).
103	
104	    The server is asked for tokens as token IDs (`return_tokens_as_token_ids`), so every token is a `"token_id:<id>"`
105	    string. Entries are sorted by descending probability, which matches the rank ordering used by vLLM.
106	
107	    Args:
108	        choices_logprobs (`list[dict]`):
109	            Logprobs of each choice, either `{"tokens": ..., "top_logprobs": ...}` (completions) or `{"content":
110	            [{"token": ..., "logprob": ..., "top_logprobs": ...}]}` (chat completions and token IDs).
111	
112	    Returns:
113	        Tuple of (logprobs, logprob_token_ids), or `(None, None)` when the server returned no logprob.
114	    """
115	    if choices_logprobs[0] is None:
116	        return None, None
117	
118	    all_logprobs = []
119	    all_token_ids = []
120	    for logprobs in choices_logprobs:
121	        if "content" in logprobs:  # chat completions
122	            positions = [
123	                (entry["token"], entry["logprob"], {top["token"]: top["logprob"] for top in entry["top_logprobs"]})
124	                for entry in logprobs["content"]
125	            ]
126	        else:  # completions
127	            positions = list(
128	                zip(logprobs["tokens"], logprobs["token_logprobs"], logprobs["top_logprobs"], strict=True)
129	            )
130	
131	        seq_logprobs = []
132	        seq_token_ids = []
133	        for token, logprob, top_logprobs in positions:
134	            # The sampled token is always included, even when it falls outside the top-N.
135	            top_logprobs = {token: logprob, **(top_logprobs or {})}
136	            items = sorted(top_logprobs.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
137	            seq_token_ids.append([int(token.removeprefix("token_id:")) for token, _ in items])
138	            seq_logprobs.append([None if math.isnan(logprob) else logprob for _, logprob in items])
139	        all_logprobs.append(seq_logprobs)
140	        all_token_ids.append(seq_token_ids)
141	    return all_logprobs, all_token_ids

144	class VLLMClient:
145	    """
146	    A client class to interact with a vLLM server.
147	
148	    This class provides methods to generate completions, initialize and manage weight update groups, and update model
149	    weights in a distributed setting. Before using it, start a vLLM server with `vllm serve`, see the vLLM integration
150	    guide for the required flags.
151	
152	    Args:
153	        base_url (`str`, *optional*):
154	            Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., `"http://localhost:8000"`). If provided, `host` and `server_port` are
155	            ignored.
156	        host (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"0.0.0.0"`):
157	            IP address of the vLLM server. Ignored if `base_url` is provided.
158	        server_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `8000`):
159	            Port number of the vLLM server. Ignored if `base_url` is provided.
160	        group_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `51216`):
161	            Port number for the weight update group.
162	        connection_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
163	            Total timeout duration in seconds to wait for the server to be up. If the server is not up after the
164	            timeout, a `ConnectionError` is raised.
165	
166	    Examples:
167	        Run the vLLM server with the model `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`:
168	
169	        ```
170	        $ VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}' \
171	              --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs -1
172	        ...
173	        INFO:     Application startup complete.
174	        INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
175	        ```
176	
177	        Use the client to generate completions and update model weights:
178	
179	        ```python
180	        >>> from trl.generation.vllm_client import VLLMClient
181	
182	        >>> client = VLLMClient()
183	        >>> client.generate(["Hello, AI!", "Tell me a joke"])
184	        {'prompt_ids': [[9707, 11, 15235, 0],
185	                        [40451, 752, 264, 21646]],
186	         'completion_ids': [[2980, 498, 1492, 752, 448, 264, 13027, 8645, 30, 358, 2776, 4460, 311, 3270, 264, 2025],
187	                            [911, 98072, 2142, 624, 45, 51426, 2142, 374, 279, 16396, 429, 4302, 702, 36988, 7290, 476]],
188	         'logprobs': [[[-1.6612], [-0.0081], [-1.5189], [-0.0123], [-1.2045], [-0.6227], [-2.9791], [-2.8387], [-0.1267], [-0.0366], [-2.6528], [-0.3197], [-0.0001], [-1.8174], [-0.0251], [-1.473]],
189	                      [[-0.018], [-10.7331], [-0.1605], [-0.891], [-3.7945], [-0.0127], [-0.3073], [-1.1648], [-1.8025], [-0.409], [-0.0256], [-1.6127], [-2.2935], [-4.1785], [-0.6531], [-0.2629]]],
190	         'logprob_token_ids': [[[2980], [498], [1492], [752], [448], [264], [13027], [8645], [30], [358], [2776], [4460], [311], [3270], [264], [2025]],
191	                               [[911], [98072], [2142], [624], [45], [51426], [2142], [374], [279], [16396], [429], [4302], [702], [36988], [7290], [476]]]}
192	
193	        >>> from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
194	
195	        >>> model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B", device_map="cuda")
196	        >>> client.init_communicator(device="cuda")
197	        >>> client.update_model_params(model)
198	        ```
199	
200	        There are several ways to initialize the client:
201	
202	        ```python
203	        >>> VLLMClient(base_url="http://localhost:8000")
204	        >>> VLLMClient(base_url="http://192.168.1.100:8000")
205	        >>> VLLMClient(host="localhost", server_port=8000)
206	        >>> VLLMClient(host="192.168.1.100", server_port=8000)
207	        ```
208	    """
209	
210	    def __init__(
211	        self,
212	        base_url: str | None = None,
213	        host: str = "0.0.0.0",
214	        server_port: int = 8000,
215	        group_port: int = 51216,
216	        connection_timeout: float = 0.0,
217	    ):
218	        if not is_requests_available():
219	            raise ImportError("requests is not installed. Please install it with `pip install requests`.")
220	        if not is_vllm_available():
221	            raise ImportError("vLLM is not installed. Please install it with `pip install trl[vllm]`.")
222	
223	        self.session = requests.Session()
224	
225	        # Configure retries for HTTP requests made through this session.
226	        # This is not strictly required for correctness, but it helps make training more robust to rare, transient
227	        # failures (network hiccups, temporary 5xx errors, overloaded servers). Without this, such failures could cause
228	        # an otherwise healthy training run to fail.
229	        retry_strategy = Retry(
230	            total=5,  # global cap on the total number of retries across all failure types
231	            connect=5,  # retry connection-level failures (DNS issues, refused connections, etc)
232	            read=5,  # retry failures while reading the response after the connection was successfully established
233	            status=3,  # retry a limited number of times when we receive certain HTTP error responses from the server
234	            status_forcelist=[500, 502, 503],  # only retry on server-side errors that are usually temporary
235	            backoff_factor=2,  # exponential backoff between retries (2s, 4s, 8s, ...)
236	            allowed_methods=["POST", "GET"],  # allow POST as well, even though we're not sure it's safe here
237	        )
238	
239	        # Match the default generation concurrency so connections can be reused across batches.
240	        adapter = HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry_strategy, pool_maxsize=_DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY)
241	        self.session.mount("http://", adapter)
242	        self.session.mount("https://", adapter)
243	
244	        if base_url is not None:
245	            # Parse the base_url to extract host and port
246	            parsed_url = urlparse(base_url)
247	            self.host = socket.gethostbyname(parsed_url.hostname)
248	            scheme = parsed_url.scheme or "http"
249	            self.base_url = f"{scheme}://{parsed_url.netloc}{parsed_url.path}"
250	        else:
251	            self.host = host
252	            self.server_port = server_port
253	            self.base_url = f"http://{self.host}:{self.server_port}"
254	        self.group_port = group_port
255	        self.communicator = None
256	        self._updating_weights = False  # set while inside `weight_update`
257	        self.check_server(connection_timeout)  # check server and fail after timeout
258	        self.model = self._get(f"{self.base_url}/v1/models")["data"][0]["id"]
259	
260	    def _get(self, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
261	        response = self.session.get(url, **kwargs)
262	        if response.status_code != 200:
263	            raise Exception(f"Request failed: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
264	        return response.json()
265	
266	    def _post(self, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
267	        response = self.session.post(url, **kwargs)
268	        if response.status_code != 200:
269	            raise Exception(f"Request failed: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
270	        return response.json()
271	
272	    def check_server(self, total_timeout: float = 0.0, retry_interval: float = 2.0):
273	        """
274	        Check server availability with retries on failure, within a total timeout duration. If the server is not up
275	        after the total timeout duration, raise a `ConnectionError`.
276	
277	        Args:
278	            retry_interval (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
279	                Interval in seconds between retries.
280	            total_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
281	                Total timeout duration in seconds.
282	        """
283	        url = f"{self.base_url}/health"
284	        start_time = time.time()  # Record the start time
285	
286	        while True:
287	            try:
288	                response = requests.get(url)
289	            except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
290	                # Check if the total timeout duration has passed
291	                elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
292	                if elapsed_time >= total_timeout:
293	                    raise ConnectionError(
294	                        f"The vLLM server can't be reached at {self.base_url} after {total_timeout} seconds. Make "
295	                        "sure the server is running by running `vllm serve`."
296	                    ) from exc
297	            else:
298	                if response.status_code == 200:
299	                    if "X-Forwarded-For" in response.headers:
300	                        self.host = response.headers["X-Forwarded-For"]
301	                    logger.info("Server is up!")
302	                    return
303	
304	            # Retry logic: wait before trying again
305	            logger.info(f"Server is not up yet. Retrying in {retry_interval} seconds...")
306	            time.sleep(retry_interval)

310	        Returns the number of workers of the vLLM server, i.e. `tensor_parallel_size * data_parallel_size`.
311	        """
312	        return self._get(f"{self.base_url}/get_world_size")["world_size"]

314	    def image_features(
315	        self, images: list[list | None], max_concurrent_requests: int = _DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY
316	    ) -> list[dict | None]:
317	        """
318	        Processes images server-side into the features that pair with token IDs in
319	        [`~generation.vllm_client.VLLMClient.generate`].
320	
321	        The server generates from either token IDs or images, never both, so images are sent on their own first. The
322	        features it returns carry the processed image data and its hashes, which depend on the image alone, and stay
323	        valid for any token sequence they are paired with.
324	
325	        Args:
326	            images (`list[list[PIL.Image] | None]`):
327	                List of image lists for VLM support. Each element is a list of PIL images for the corresponding prompt,
328	                or `None` if no images for that prompt.
329	            max_concurrent_requests (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `64`):
330	                Maximum number of prompts processed at the same time, as the endpoint takes one at a time.
331	
332	        Returns:
333	            `list[dict]`: Processed image data for each prompt, `None` where the prompt had no image.
334	        """
335	
336	        def send(images_for_prompt):
337	            if not images_for_prompt:
338	                return None
339	            messages = [
340	                {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": image} for image in images_for_prompt]}
341	            ]
342	            rendered = self._post(
343	                f"{self.base_url}/v1/chat/completions/render",
344	                json={"model": self.model, "messages": to_openai_messages(messages), "max_tokens": 1},
345	            )
346	            return rendered["features"]
347	
348	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(max_concurrent_requests, len(images))) as executor:
349	            return list(executor.map(send, images))
350	
351	    def generate(
352	        self,
353	        prompts: list[str] | list[list[int]],
354	        features: list[dict | None] | None = None,
355	        n: int = 1,
356	        repetition_penalty: float = 1.0,
357	        temperature: float = 1.0,
358	        top_p: float = 1.0,
359	        top_k: int = 0,
360	        min_p: float = 0.0,
361	        max_tokens: int = 16,
362	        logprobs: int | None = 0,
363	        structured_outputs_regex: str | None = None,
364	        generation_kwargs: dict | None = None,
365	    ) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
366	        """
367	        Generates model completions for the provided prompts.
368	
369	        Args:
370	            prompts (`list[str]` or `list[list[int]]`):
371	                List of text prompts or list of token ID lists for which the model will generate completions.
372	            features (`list[dict]`, *optional*):
373	                Processed image data from [`~generation.vllm_client.VLLMClient.image_features`], one per prompt (`None`
374	                for prompts without images). When provided, prompts must be token IDs.
375	            n (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
376	                Number of completions to generate for each prompt.
377	            repetition_penalty (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
378	                Parameter for repetition penalty. 1.0 means no penalty.
379	            temperature (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
380	                Temperature parameter for sampling. Higher values increase diversity.
381	            top_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
382	                Top-p sampling parameter.`1.0` means no truncation.
383	            top_k (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):
384	                Top-k sampling parameter. `0` means no truncation.
385	            min_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
386	                Minimum probability for sampling.
387	            max_tokens (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `16`):
388	                Maximum number of tokens to generate for each prompt.
389	            logprobs (`int` or `None`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):
390	                Number of top logprobs to return per token. When 0, only the sampled token's logprob is returned. When
391	                N>0, returns up to N+1 logprobs sorted by descending probability, because vLLM always includes the
392	                sampled token's logprob (which may fall outside the top-N). When `None`, no logprob is returned.
393	            structured_outputs_regex (`str`, *optional*):
394	                Regular expression to guide the decoding process.
395	            generation_kwargs (`dict`, *optional*):
396	                Additional generation parameters, passed as-is in the request body. This can include parameters like
397	                `seed`, `frequency_penalty`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict with the other parameters, they
398	                will override them.
399	
400	        Returns:
401	            `dict` with keys:
402	                - `prompt_ids` (`list[list[int]]`):
403	                    List of lists of token IDs representing the tokenized input prompts.
404	                - `completion_ids` (`list[list[int]]`):
405	                    List of lists of token IDs representing the model-generated completions for each prompt.
406	                - `logprobs` (`list[list[list[float]]]`):
407	                    Per-token logprobs of shape (num_sequences, seq_len, num_logprobs), sorted by descending
408	                    probability.
409	                - `logprob_token_ids` (`list[list[list[int]]]`):
410	                    Token IDs corresponding to each logprob, same shape as `logprobs`.
411	        """
412	        sampling_params = {
413	            "n": n,
414	            "repetition_penalty": repetition_penalty,
415	            "temperature": temperature,
416	            "top_p": top_p,
417	            "top_k": top_k,
418	            "min_p": min_p,
419	            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
420	            "logprobs": logprobs,
421	        }
422	        if structured_outputs_regex is not None:
423	            sampling_params["structured_outputs"] = {"regex": structured_outputs_regex}
424	        sampling_params.update(generation_kwargs or {})
425	
426	        if features is not None:
427	            return self._generate_from_features(prompts, features, sampling_params)
428	
429	        payload = {
430	            "model": self.model,
431	            "prompt": prompts,
432	            "return_token_ids": True,
433	            "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True,
434	            **sampling_params,
435	        }
436	        choices = self._post(f"{self.base_url}/v1/completions", json=payload)["choices"]
437	
438	        # Choices are returned prompt-major: the n completions of a prompt come before those of the next prompt.
439	        prompt_ids = [choice["prompt_token_ids"] for choice in choices[::n]]
440	        completion_ids = [choice["token_ids"] for choice in choices]
441	        logprobs, logprob_token_ids = parse_logprobs([choice["logprobs"] for choice in choices])
442	        return {
443	            "prompt_ids": prompt_ids,
444	            "completion_ids": completion_ids,
445	            "logprobs": logprobs,
446	            "logprob_token_ids": logprob_token_ids,
447	        }
448	
449	    def _generate_from_features(
450	        self,
451	        prompts: list[list[int]],
452	        features: list[dict | None],
453	        sampling_params: dict,
454	        max_concurrent_requests: int = _DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY,
455	    ) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
456	        """Generate from token IDs paired with multimodal features, one request per prompt."""
457	        # The server leaves the default output kind on non-streaming requests, under which it returns only the
458	        # sequences that finished last, silently dropping the others when n > 1. See vLLM PR #52399.
459	        sampling_params = {**sampling_params, "output_kind": 2}  # FINAL_ONLY
460	
461	        def send(index):
462	            return self._post(
463	                f"{self.base_url}/inference/v1/generate",
464	                json={
465	                    "request_id": f"trl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
466	                    "model": self.model,
467	                    "token_ids": prompts[index],
468	                    "features": features[index],
469	                    "sampling_params": sampling_params,
470	                },
471	            )
472	
473	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(max_concurrent_requests, len(prompts))) as executor:
474	            responses = list(executor.map(send, range(len(prompts))))
475	
476	        choices = [choice for response in responses for choice in response["choices"]]
477	        logprobs, logprob_token_ids = parse_logprobs([choice["logprobs"] for choice in choices])
478	        return {
479	            "prompt_ids": list(prompts),  # the server generates from what it was given, so it echoes back unchanged
480	            "completion_ids": [choice["token_ids"] for choice in choices],
481	            "logprobs": logprobs,
482	            "logprob_token_ids": logprob_token_ids,
483	        }

# with an empty body.

_DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY = 64


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def pil_to_base64(image):
    buffer = BytesIO()
    image.save(buffer, format="PNG")
    img_bytes = buffer.getvalue()
    return base64.b64encode(img_bytes).decode("utf-8")


def to_openai_messages(messages: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Convert TRL-style messages to the OpenAI format understood by the vLLM server, by inlining images as data URLs.

    Args:
        messages (`list[dict]`):
            Messages whose content parts may be `{"type": "image", "image": <PIL.Image>}` or `{"type": "image_pil",
            "image_pil": <PIL.Image>}`.

    Returns:
        `list[dict]`: Messages with image parts replaced by `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:..."}}`.
    """
    messages = copy.deepcopy(messages)
    for message in messages:
        if isinstance(message["content"], list):
            for idx, part in enumerate(message["content"]):
                key = "image" if part["type"] == "image" else "image_pil" if part["type"] == "image_pil" else None
                if key is not None:
                    url = f"data:image/png;base64,{pil_to_base64(part[key])}"
                    message["content"][idx] = {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": url}}
    return messages


def parse_logprobs(choices_logprobs: list[dict | None]) -> tuple[list | None, list | None]:
    """
    Parse the logprobs of a batch of choices into two lists of shape (num_sequences, seq_len, num_logprobs).

    The server is asked for tokens as token IDs (`return_tokens_as_token_ids`), so every token is a `"token_id:<id>"`
    string. Entries are sorted by descending probability, which matches the rank ordering used by vLLM.

    Args:
        choices_logprobs (`list[dict]`):
            Logprobs of each choice, either `{"tokens": ..., "top_logprobs": ...}` (completions) or `{"content":
            [{"token": ..., "logprob": ..., "top_logprobs": ...}]}` (chat completions and token IDs).

    Returns:
        Tuple of (logprobs, logprob_token_ids), or `(None, None)` when the server returned no logprob.
    """
    if choices_logprobs[0] is None:
        return None, None

    all_logprobs = []
    all_token_ids = []
    for logprobs in choices_logprobs:
        if "content" in logprobs:  # chat completions
            positions = [
                (entry["token"], entry["logprob"], {top["token"]: top["logprob"] for top in entry["top_logprobs"]})
                for entry in logprobs["content"]
            ]
        else:  # completions
            positions = list(
                zip(logprobs["tokens"], logprobs["token_logprobs"], logprobs["top_logprobs"], strict=True)
            )

        seq_logprobs = []
        seq_token_ids = []
        for token, logprob, top_logprobs in positions:
            # The sampled token is always included, even when it falls outside the top-N.
            top_logprobs = {token: logprob, **(top_logprobs or {})}
            items = sorted(top_logprobs.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
            seq_token_ids.append([int(token.removeprefix("token_id:")) for token, _ in items])
            seq_logprobs.append([None if math.isnan(logprob) else logprob for _, logprob in items])
        all_logprobs.append(seq_logprobs)
        all_token_ids.append(seq_token_ids)
    return all_logprobs, all_token_ids


class VLLMClient:
    """
    A client class to interact with a vLLM server.

    This class provides methods to generate completions, initialize and manage weight update groups, and update model
    weights in a distributed setting. Before using it, start a vLLM server with `vllm serve`, see the vLLM integration
    guide for the required flags.

    Args:
        base_url (`str`, *optional*):
            Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., `"http://localhost:8000"`). If provided, `host` and `server_port` are
            ignored.
        host (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"0.0.0.0"`):
            IP address of the vLLM server. Ignored if `base_url` is provided.
        server_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `8000`):
            Port number of the vLLM server. Ignored if `base_url` is provided.
        group_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `51216`):
            Port number for the weight update group.
        connection_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
            Total timeout duration in seconds to wait for the server to be up. If the server is not up after the
            timeout, a `ConnectionError` is raised.

    Examples:
        Run the vLLM server with the model `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`:

        ```
        $ VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}' \
              --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs -1
        ...
        INFO:     Application startup complete.
        INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
        ```

        Use the client to generate completions and update model weights:

        ```python
        >>> from trl.generation.vllm_client import VLLMClient

        >>> client = VLLMClient()
        >>> client.generate(["Hello, AI!", "Tell me a joke"])
        {'prompt_ids': [[9707, 11, 15235, 0],
                        [40451, 752, 264, 21646]],
         'completion_ids': [[2980, 498, 1492, 752, 448, 264, 13027, 8645, 30, 358, 2776, 4460, 311, 3270, 264, 2025],
                            [911, 98072, 2142, 624, 45, 51426, 2142, 374, 279, 16396, 429, 4302, 702, 36988, 7290, 476]],
         'logprobs': [[[-1.6612], [-0.0081], [-1.5189], [-0.0123], [-1.2045], [-0.6227], [-2.9791], [-2.8387], [-0.1267], [-0.0366], [-2.6528], [-0.3197], [-0.0001], [-1.8174], [-0.0251], [-1.473]],
                      [[-0.018], [-10.7331], [-0.1605], [-0.891], [-3.7945], [-0.0127], [-0.3073], [-1.1648], [-1.8025], [-0.409], [-0.0256], [-1.6127], [-2.2935], [-4.1785], [-0.6531], [-0.2629]]],
         'logprob_token_ids': [[[2980], [498], [1492], [752], [448], [264], [13027], [8645], [30], [358], [2776], [4460], [311], [3270], [264], [2025]],
                               [[911], [98072], [2142], [624], [45], [51426], [2142], [374], [279], [16396], [429], [4302], [702], [36988], [7290], [476]]]}

        >>> from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

        >>> model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B", device_map="cuda")
        >>> client.init_communicator(device="cuda")
        >>> client.update_model_params(model)
        ```

        There are several ways to initialize the client:

        ```python
        >>> VLLMClient(base_url="http://localhost:8000")
        >>> VLLMClient(base_url="http://192.168.1.100:8000")
        >>> VLLMClient(host="localhost", server_port=8000)
        >>> VLLMClient(host="192.168.1.100", server_port=8000)
        ```
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        host: str = "0.0.0.0",
        server_port: int = 8000,
        group_port: int = 51216,
        connection_timeout: float = 0.0,
    ):
        if not is_requests_available():
            raise ImportError("requests is not installed. Please install it with `pip install requests`.")
        if not is_vllm_available():
            raise ImportError("vLLM is not installed. Please install it with `pip install trl[vllm]`.")

        self.session = requests.Session()

        # Configure retries for HTTP requests made through this session.
        # This is not strictly required for correctness, but it helps make training more robust to rare, transient
        # failures (network hiccups, temporary 5xx errors, overloaded servers). Without this, such failures could cause
        # an otherwise healthy training run to fail.
        retry_strategy = Retry(
            total=5,  # global cap on the total number of retries across all failure types
            connect=5,  # retry connection-level failures (DNS issues, refused connections, etc)
            read=5,  # retry failures while reading the response after the connection was successfully established
            status=3,  # retry a limited number of times when we receive certain HTTP error responses from the server
            status_forcelist=[500, 502, 503],  # only retry on server-side errors that are usually temporary
            backoff_factor=2,  # exponential backoff between retries (2s, 4s, 8s, ...)
            allowed_methods=["POST", "GET"],  # allow POST as well, even though we're not sure it's safe here
        )

        # Match the default generation concurrency so connections can be reused across batches.
        adapter = HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry_strategy, pool_maxsize=_DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY)
        self.session.mount("http://", adapter)
        self.session.mount("https://", adapter)

        if base_url is not None:
            # Parse the base_url to extract host and port
            parsed_url = urlparse(base_url)
            self.host = socket.gethostbyname(parsed_url.hostname)
            scheme = parsed_url.scheme or "http"
            self.base_url = f"{scheme}://{parsed_url.netloc}{parsed_url.path}"
        else:
            self.host = host
            self.server_port = server_port
            self.base_url = f"http://{self.host}:{self.server_port}"
        self.group_port = group_port
        self.communicator = None
        self._updating_weights = False  # set while inside `weight_update`
        self.check_server(connection_timeout)  # check server and fail after timeout
        self.model = self._get(f"{self.base_url}/v1/models")["data"][0]["id"]

    def _get(self, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
        response = self.session.get(url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code != 200:
            raise Exception(f"Request failed: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
        return response.json()

    def _post(self, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
        response = self.session.post(url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code != 200:
            raise Exception(f"Request failed: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
        return response.json()

    def check_server(self, total_timeout: float = 0.0, retry_interval: float = 2.0):
        """
        Check server availability with retries on failure, within a total timeout duration. If the server is not up
        after the total timeout duration, raise a `ConnectionError`.

        Args:
            retry_interval (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
                Interval in seconds between retries.
            total_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
                Total timeout duration in seconds.
        """
        url = f"{self.base_url}/health"
        start_time = time.time()  # Record the start time

        while True:
            try:
                response = requests.get(url)
            except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
                # Check if the total timeout duration has passed
                elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
                if elapsed_time >= total_timeout:
                    raise ConnectionError(
                        f"The vLLM server can't be reached at {self.base_url} after {total_timeout} seconds. Make "
                        "sure the server is running by running `vllm serve`."
                    ) from exc
            else:
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    if "X-Forwarded-For" in response.headers:
                        self.host = response.headers["X-Forwarded-For"]
                    logger.info("Server is up!")
                    return

            # Retry logic: wait before trying again
            logger.info(f"Server is not up yet. Retrying in {retry_interval} seconds...")
            time.sleep(retry_interval)

    def get_world_size(self) -> int:
        """
        Returns the number of workers of the vLLM server, i.e. `tensor_parallel_size * data_parallel_size`.
        """
        return self._get(f"{self.base_url}/get_world_size")["world_size"]

    def image_features(
        self, images: list[list | None], max_concurrent_requests: int = _DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY
    ) -> list[dict | None]:
        """
        Processes images server-side into the features that pair with token IDs in
        [`~generation.vllm_client.VLLMClient.generate`].

        The server generates from either token IDs or images, never both, so images are sent on their own first. The
        features it returns carry the processed image data and its hashes, which depend on the image alone, and stay
        valid for any token sequence they are paired with.

        Args:
            images (`list[list[PIL.Image] | None]`):
                List of image lists for VLM support. Each element is a list of PIL images for the corresponding prompt,
                or `None` if no images for that prompt.
            max_concurrent_requests (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `64`):
                Maximum number of prompts processed at the same time, as the endpoint takes one at a time.

        Returns:
            `list[dict]`: Processed image data for each prompt, `None` where the prompt had no image.
        """

        def send(images_for_prompt):
            if not images_for_prompt:
                return None
            messages = [
                {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": image} for image in images_for_prompt]}
            ]
            rendered = self._post(
                f"{self.base_url}/v1/chat/completions/render",
                json={"model": self.model, "messages": to_openai_messages(messages), "max_tokens": 1},
            )
            return rendered["features"]

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(max_concurrent_requests, len(images))) as executor:
            return list(executor.map(send, images))

    def generate(
        self,
        prompts: list[str] | list[list[int]],
        features: list[dict | None] | None = None,
        n: int = 1,
        repetition_penalty: float = 1.0,
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        top_p: float = 1.0,
        top_k: int = 0,
        min_p: float = 0.0,
        max_tokens: int = 16,
        logprobs: int | None = 0,
        structured_outputs_regex: str | None = None,
        generation_kwargs: dict | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
        """
        Generates model completions for the provided prompts.

        Args:
            prompts (`list[str]` or `list[list[int]]`):
                List of text prompts or list of token ID lists for which the model will generate completions.
            features (`list[dict]`, *optional*):
                Processed image data from [`~generation.vllm_client.VLLMClient.image_features`], one per prompt (`None`
                for prompts without images). When provided, prompts must be token IDs.
            n (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
                Number of completions to generate for each prompt.
            repetition_penalty (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
                Parameter for repetition penalty. 1.0 means no penalty.
            temperature (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
                Temperature parameter for sampling. Higher values increase diversity.
            top_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
                Top-p sampling parameter.`1.0` means no truncation.
            top_k (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):
                Top-k sampling parameter. `0` means no truncation.
            min_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
                Minimum probability for sampling.
            max_tokens (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `16`):
                Maximum number of tokens to generate for each prompt.
            logprobs (`int` or `None`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):
                Number of top logprobs to return per token. When 0, only the sampled token's logprob is returned. When
                N>0, returns up to N+1 logprobs sorted by descending probability, because vLLM always includes the
                sampled token's logprob (which may fall outside the top-N). When `None`, no logprob is returned.
            structured_outputs_regex (`str`, *optional*):
                Regular expression to guide the decoding process.
            generation_kwargs (`dict`, *optional*):
                Additional generation parameters, passed as-is in the request body. This can include parameters like
                `seed`, `frequency_penalty`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict with the other parameters, they
                will override them.

        Returns:
            `dict` with keys:
                - `prompt_ids` (`list[list[int]]`):
                    List of lists of token IDs representing the tokenized input prompts.
                - `completion_ids` (`list[list[int]]`):
                    List of lists of token IDs representing the model-generated completions for each prompt.
                - `logprobs` (`list[list[list[float]]]`):
                    Per-token logprobs of shape (num_sequences, seq_len, num_logprobs), sorted by descending
                    probability.
                - `logprob_token_ids` (`list[list[list[int]]]`):
                    Token IDs corresponding to each logprob, same shape as `logprobs`.
        """
        sampling_params = {
            "n": n,
            "repetition_penalty": repetition_penalty,
            "temperature": temperature,
            "top_p": top_p,
            "top_k": top_k,
            "min_p": min_p,
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "logprobs": logprobs,
        }
        if structured_outputs_regex is not None:
            sampling_params["structured_outputs"] = {"regex": structured_outputs_regex}
        sampling_params.update(generation_kwargs or {})

        if features is not None:
            return self._generate_from_features(prompts, features, sampling_params)

        payload = {
            "model": self.model,
            "prompt": prompts,
            "return_token_ids": True,
            "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True,
            **sampling_params,
        }
        choices = self._post(f"{self.base_url}/v1/completions", json=payload)["choices"]

        # Choices are returned prompt-major: the n completions of a prompt come before those of the next prompt.
        prompt_ids = [choice["prompt_token_ids"] for choice in choices[::n]]
        completion_ids = [choice["token_ids"] for choice in choices]
        logprobs, logprob_token_ids = parse_logprobs([choice["logprobs"] for choice in choices])
        return {
            "prompt_ids": prompt_ids,
            "completion_ids": completion_ids,
            "logprobs": logprobs,
            "logprob_token_ids": logprob_token_ids,
        }

    def _generate_from_features(
        self,
        prompts: list[list[int]],
        features: list[dict | None],
        sampling_params: dict,
        max_concurrent_requests: int = _DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY,
    ) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
        """Generate from token IDs paired with multimodal features, one request per prompt."""
        # The server leaves the default output kind on non-streaming requests, under which it returns only the
        # sequences that finished last, silently dropping the others when n > 1. See vLLM PR #52399.
        sampling_params = {**sampling_params, "output_kind": 2}  # FINAL_ONLY

        def send(index):
            return self._post(
                f"{self.base_url}/inference/v1/generate",
                json={
                    "request_id": f"trl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
                    "model": self.model,
                    "token_ids": prompts[index],
                    "features": features[index],
                    "sampling_params": sampling_params,
                },
            )

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(max_concurrent_requests, len(prompts))) as executor:
            responses = list(executor.map(send, range(len(prompts))))

        choices = [choice for response in responses for choice in response["choices"]]
        logprobs, logprob_token_ids = parse_logprobs([choice["logprobs"] for choice in choices])
        return {
            "prompt_ids": list(prompts),  # the server generates from what it was given, so it echoes back unchanged
            "completion_ids": [choice["token_ids"] for choice in choices],
            "logprobs": logprobs,
            "logprob_token_ids": logprob_token_ids,
        }

    def chat(
        self,
        messages: list[list[dict]],
        n: int = 1,
        repetition_penalty: float = 1.0,
        temperature: float = 1.0,
        top_p: float = 1.0,
        top_k: int = 0,
        min_p: float = 0.0,
        max_tokens: int = 16,

        structured_outputs_regex: str | None = None,
        generation_kwargs: dict | None = None,
        chat_template_kwargs: dict | None = None,
        tools: list | None = None,

115	    if choices_logprobs[0] is None:
116	        return None, None
117	
118	    all_logprobs = []
119	    all_token_ids = []
120	    for logprobs in choices_logprobs:
121	        if "content" in logprobs:  # chat completions
122	            positions = [
123	                (entry["token"], entry["logprob"], {top["token"]: top["logprob"] for top in entry["top_logprobs"]})
124	                for entry in logprobs["content"]
125	            ]
126	        else:  # completions
127	            positions = list(
128	                zip(logprobs["tokens"], logprobs["token_logprobs"], logprobs["top_logprobs"], strict=True)
129	            )
130	
131	        seq_logprobs = []
132	        seq_token_ids = []
133	        for token, logprob, top_logprobs in positions:
134	            # The sampled token is always included, even when it falls outside the top-N.
135	            top_logprobs = {token: logprob, **(top_logprobs or {})}
136	            items = sorted(top_logprobs.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
137	            seq_token_ids.append([int(token.removeprefix("token_id:")) for token, _ in items])
138	            seq_logprobs.append([None if math.isnan(logprob) else logprob for _, logprob in items])
139	        all_logprobs.append(seq_logprobs)
140	        all_token_ids.append(seq_token_ids)
141	    return all_logprobs, all_token_ids

145	    """
146	    A client class to interact with a vLLM server.
147	
148	    This class provides methods to generate completions, initialize and manage weight update groups, and update model
149	    weights in a distributed setting. Before using it, start a vLLM server with `vllm serve`, see the vLLM integration
150	    guide for the required flags.
151	
152	    Args:
153	        base_url (`str`, *optional*):
154	            Base URL for the vLLM server (e.g., `"http://localhost:8000"`). If provided, `host` and `server_port` are
155	            ignored.
156	        host (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"0.0.0.0"`):
157	            IP address of the vLLM server. Ignored if `base_url` is provided.
158	        server_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `8000`):
159	            Port number of the vLLM server. Ignored if `base_url` is provided.
160	        group_port (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `51216`):
161	            Port number for the weight update group.
162	        connection_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
163	            Total timeout duration in seconds to wait for the server to be up. If the server is not up after the
164	            timeout, a `ConnectionError` is raised.
165	
166	    Examples:
167	        Run the vLLM server with the model `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`:
168	
169	        ```
170	        $ VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}' \
171	              --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --max-logprobs -1
172	        ...
173	        INFO:     Application startup complete.
174	        INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
175	        ```
176	
177	        Use the client to generate completions and update model weights:
178	
179	        ```python
180	        >>> from trl.generation.vllm_client import VLLMClient
181	
182	        >>> client = VLLMClient()
183	        >>> client.generate(["Hello, AI!", "Tell me a joke"])
184	        {'prompt_ids': [[9707, 11, 15235, 0],
185	                        [40451, 752, 264, 21646]],
186	         'completion_ids': [[2980, 498, 1492, 752, 448, 264, 13027, 8645, 30, 358, 2776, 4460, 311, 3270, 264, 2025],
187	                            [911, 98072, 2142, 624, 45, 51426, 2142, 374, 279, 16396, 429, 4302, 702, 36988, 7290, 476]],
188	         'logprobs': [[[-1.6612], [-0.0081], [-1.5189], [-0.0123], [-1.2045], [-0.6227], [-2.9791], [-2.8387], [-0.1267], [-0.0366], [-2.6528], [-0.3197], [-0.0001], [-1.8174], [-0.0251], [-1.473]],
189	                      [[-0.018], [-10.7331], [-0.1605], [-0.891], [-3.7945], [-0.0127], [-0.3073], [-1.1648], [-1.8025], [-0.409], [-0.0256], [-1.6127], [-2.2935], [-4.1785], [-0.6531], [-0.2629]]],
190	         'logprob_token_ids': [[[2980], [498], [1492], [752], [448], [264], [13027], [8645], [30], [358], [2776], [4460], [311], [3270], [264], [2025]],
191	                               [[911], [98072], [2142], [624], [45], [51426], [2142], [374], [279], [16396], [429], [4302], [702], [36988], [7290], [476]]]}
192	
193	        >>> from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
194	
195	        >>> model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B", device_map="cuda")
196	        >>> client.init_communicator(device="cuda")
197	        >>> client.update_model_params(model)
198	        ```
199	
200	        There are several ways to initialize the client:
201	
202	        ```python
203	        >>> VLLMClient(base_url="http://localhost:8000")
204	        >>> VLLMClient(base_url="http://192.168.1.100:8000")
205	        >>> VLLMClient(host="localhost", server_port=8000)
206	        >>> VLLMClient(host="192.168.1.100", server_port=8000)
207	        ```
208	    """
209	
210	    def __init__(
211	        self,
212	        base_url: str | None = None,
213	        host: str = "0.0.0.0",
214	        server_port: int = 8000,
215	        group_port: int = 51216,
216	        connection_timeout: float = 0.0,
217	    ):
218	        if not is_requests_available():
219	            raise ImportError("requests is not installed. Please install it with `pip install requests`.")
220	        if not is_vllm_available():
221	            raise ImportError("vLLM is not installed. Please install it with `pip install trl[vllm]`.")
222	
223	        self.session = requests.Session()
224	
225	        # Configure retries for HTTP requests made through this session.
226	        # This is not strictly required for correctness, but it helps make training more robust to rare, transient
227	        # failures (network hiccups, temporary 5xx errors, overloaded servers). Without this, such failures could cause
228	        # an otherwise healthy training run to fail.
229	        retry_strategy = Retry(
230	            total=5,  # global cap on the total number of retries across all failure types
231	            connect=5,  # retry connection-level failures (DNS issues, refused connections, etc)
232	            read=5,  # retry failures while reading the response after the connection was successfully established
233	            status=3,  # retry a limited number of times when we receive certain HTTP error responses from the server
234	            status_forcelist=[500, 502, 503],  # only retry on server-side errors that are usually temporary
235	            backoff_factor=2,  # exponential backoff between retries (2s, 4s, 8s, ...)
236	            allowed_methods=["POST", "GET"],  # allow POST as well, even though we're not sure it's safe here
237	        )
238	
239	        # Match the default generation concurrency so connections can be reused across batches.
240	        adapter = HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry_strategy, pool_maxsize=_DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY)
241	        self.session.mount("http://", adapter)
242	        self.session.mount("https://", adapter)
243	
244	        if base_url is not None:
245	            # Parse the base_url to extract host and port
246	            parsed_url = urlparse(base_url)
247	            self.host = socket.gethostbyname(parsed_url.hostname)
248	            scheme = parsed_url.scheme or "http"
249	            self.base_url = f"{scheme}://{parsed_url.netloc}{parsed_url.path}"
250	        else:
251	            self.host = host
252	            self.server_port = server_port
253	            self.base_url = f"http://{self.host}:{self.server_port}"
254	        self.group_port = group_port
255	        self.communicator = None
256	        self._updating_weights = False  # set while inside `weight_update`
257	        self.check_server(connection_timeout)  # check server and fail after timeout
258	        self.model = self._get(f"{self.base_url}/v1/models")["data"][0]["id"]
259	
260	    def _get(self, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
261	        response = self.session.get(url, **kwargs)
262	        if response.status_code != 200:
263	            raise Exception(f"Request failed: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
264	        return response.json()
265	
266	    def _post(self, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
267	        response = self.session.post(url, **kwargs)
268	        if response.status_code != 200:
269	            raise Exception(f"Request failed: {response.status_code}, {response.text}")
270	        return response.json()

272	    def check_server(self, total_timeout: float = 0.0, retry_interval: float = 2.0):
273	        """
274	        Check server availability with retries on failure, within a total timeout duration. If the server is not up
275	        after the total timeout duration, raise a `ConnectionError`.
276	
277	        Args:
278	            retry_interval (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `2.0`):
279	                Interval in seconds between retries.
280	            total_timeout (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
281	                Total timeout duration in seconds.
282	        """
283	        url = f"{self.base_url}/health"
284	        start_time = time.time()  # Record the start time
285	
286	        while True:
287	            try:
288	                response = requests.get(url)
289	            except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
290	                # Check if the total timeout duration has passed
291	                elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
292	                if elapsed_time >= total_timeout:
293	                    raise ConnectionError(
294	                        f"The vLLM server can't be reached at {self.base_url} after {total_timeout} seconds. Make "
295	                        "sure the server is running by running `vllm serve`."
296	                    ) from exc
297	            else:
298	                if response.status_code == 200:
299	                    if "X-Forwarded-For" in response.headers:
300	                        self.host = response.headers["X-Forwarded-For"]
301	                    logger.info("Server is up!")
302	                    return
303	
304	            # Retry logic: wait before trying again
305	            logger.info(f"Server is not up yet. Retrying in {retry_interval} seconds...")
306	            time.sleep(retry_interval)

308	    def get_world_size(self) -> int:
309	        """
310	        Returns the number of workers of the vLLM server, i.e. `tensor_parallel_size * data_parallel_size`.
311	        """
312	        return self._get(f"{self.base_url}/get_world_size")["world_size"]

314	    def image_features(
315	        self, images: list[list | None], max_concurrent_requests: int = _DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY
316	    ) -> list[dict | None]:
317	        """
318	        Processes images server-side into the features that pair with token IDs in
319	        [`~generation.vllm_client.VLLMClient.generate`].
320	
321	        The server generates from either token IDs or images, never both, so images are sent on their own first. The
322	        features it returns carry the processed image data and its hashes, which depend on the image alone, and stay
323	        valid for any token sequence they are paired with.
324	
325	        Args:
326	            images (`list[list[PIL.Image] | None]`):
327	                List of image lists for VLM support. Each element is a list of PIL images for the corresponding prompt,
328	                or `None` if no images for that prompt.
329	            max_concurrent_requests (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `64`):
330	                Maximum number of prompts processed at the same time, as the endpoint takes one at a time.
331	
332	        Returns:
333	            `list[dict]`: Processed image data for each prompt, `None` where the prompt had no image.
334	        """
335	
336	        def send(images_for_prompt):
337	            if not images_for_prompt:
338	                return None
339	            messages = [
340	                {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "image": image} for image in images_for_prompt]}
341	            ]
342	            rendered = self._post(
343	                f"{self.base_url}/v1/chat/completions/render",
344	                json={"model": self.model, "messages": to_openai_messages(messages), "max_tokens": 1},
345	            )
346	            return rendered["features"]
347	
348	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(max_concurrent_requests, len(images))) as executor:
349	            return list(executor.map(send, images))

351	    def generate(
352	        self,
353	        prompts: list[str] | list[list[int]],
354	        features: list[dict | None] | None = None,
355	        n: int = 1,
356	        repetition_penalty: float = 1.0,
357	        temperature: float = 1.0,
358	        top_p: float = 1.0,
359	        top_k: int = 0,
360	        min_p: float = 0.0,
361	        max_tokens: int = 16,
362	        logprobs: int | None = 0,
363	        structured_outputs_regex: str | None = None,
364	        generation_kwargs: dict | None = None,
365	    ) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
366	        """
367	        Generates model completions for the provided prompts.
368	
369	        Args:
370	            prompts (`list[str]` or `list[list[int]]`):
371	                List of text prompts or list of token ID lists for which the model will generate completions.
372	            features (`list[dict]`, *optional*):
373	                Processed image data from [`~generation.vllm_client.VLLMClient.image_features`], one per prompt (`None`
374	                for prompts without images). When provided, prompts must be token IDs.
375	            n (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `1`):
376	                Number of completions to generate for each prompt.
377	            repetition_penalty (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
378	                Parameter for repetition penalty. 1.0 means no penalty.
379	            temperature (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
380	                Temperature parameter for sampling. Higher values increase diversity.
381	            top_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `1.0`):
382	                Top-p sampling parameter.`1.0` means no truncation.
383	            top_k (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):
384	                Top-k sampling parameter. `0` means no truncation.
385	            min_p (`float`, *optional*, defaults to `0.0`):
386	                Minimum probability for sampling.
387	            max_tokens (`int`, *optional*, defaults to `16`):
388	                Maximum number of tokens to generate for each prompt.
389	            logprobs (`int` or `None`, *optional*, defaults to `0`):
390	                Number of top logprobs to return per token. When 0, only the sampled token's logprob is returned. When
391	                N>0, returns up to N+1 logprobs sorted by descending probability, because vLLM always includes the
392	                sampled token's logprob (which may fall outside the top-N). When `None`, no logprob is returned.
393	            structured_outputs_regex (`str`, *optional*):
394	                Regular expression to guide the decoding process.
395	            generation_kwargs (`dict`, *optional*):
396	                Additional generation parameters, passed as-is in the request body. This can include parameters like
397	                `seed`, `frequency_penalty`, etc. If it contains keys that conflict with the other parameters, they
398	                will override them.
399	
400	        Returns:
401	            `dict` with keys:
402	                - `prompt_ids` (`list[list[int]]`):
403	                    List of lists of token IDs representing the tokenized input prompts.
404	                - `completion_ids` (`list[list[int]]`):
405	                    List of lists of token IDs representing the model-generated completions for each prompt.
406	                - `logprobs` (`list[list[list[float]]]`):
407	                    Per-token logprobs of shape (num_sequences, seq_len, num_logprobs), sorted by descending
408	                    probability.
409	                - `logprob_token_ids` (`list[list[list[int]]]`):
410	                    Token IDs corresponding to each logprob, same shape as `logprobs`.
411	        """
412	        sampling_params = {
413	            "n": n,
414	            "repetition_penalty": repetition_penalty,
415	            "temperature": temperature,
416	            "top_p": top_p,
417	            "top_k": top_k,
418	            "min_p": min_p,
419	            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
420	            "logprobs": logprobs,
421	        }
422	        if structured_outputs_regex is not None:
423	            sampling_params["structured_outputs"] = {"regex": structured_outputs_regex}
424	        sampling_params.update(generation_kwargs or {})
425	
426	        if features is not None:
427	            return self._generate_from_features(prompts, features, sampling_params)
428	
429	        payload = {
430	            "model": self.model,
431	            "prompt": prompts,
432	            "return_token_ids": True,
433	            "return_tokens_as_token_ids": True,
434	            **sampling_params,
435	        }
436	        choices = self._post(f"{self.base_url}/v1/completions", json=payload)["choices"]
437	
438	        # Choices are returned prompt-major: the n completions of a prompt come before those of the next prompt.
439	        prompt_ids = [choice["prompt_token_ids"] for choice in choices[::n]]
440	        completion_ids = [choice["token_ids"] for choice in choices]
441	        logprobs, logprob_token_ids = parse_logprobs([choice["logprobs"] for choice in choices])
442	        return {
443	            "prompt_ids": prompt_ids,
444	            "completion_ids": completion_ids,
445	            "logprobs": logprobs,
446	            "logprob_token_ids": logprob_token_ids,
447	        }

449	    def _generate_from_features(
450	        self,
451	        prompts: list[list[int]],
452	        features: list[dict | None],
453	        sampling_params: dict,
454	        max_concurrent_requests: int = _DEFAULT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY,
455	    ) -> dict[str, list[list[int]]]:
456	        """Generate from token IDs paired with multimodal features, one request per prompt."""
457	        # The server leaves the default output kind on non-streaming requests, under which it returns only the
458	        # sequences that finished last, silently dropping the others when n > 1. See vLLM PR #52399.
459	        sampling_params = {**sampling_params, "output_kind": 2}  # FINAL_ONLY
460	
461	        def send(index):
462	            return self._post(
463	                f"{self.base_url}/inference/v1/generate",
464	                json={
465	                    "request_id": f"trl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
466	                    "model": self.model,
467	                    "token_ids": prompts[index],
468	                    "features": features[index],
469	                    "sampling_params": sampling_params,
470	                },
471	            )
472	
473	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(max_concurrent_requests, len(prompts))) as executor:
474	            responses = list(executor.map(send, range(len(prompts))))
475	
476	        choices = [choice for response in responses for choice in response["choices"]]
477	        logprobs, logprob_token_ids = parse_logprobs([choice["logprobs"] for choice in choices])
478	        return {
479	            "prompt_ids": list(prompts),  # the server generates from what it was given, so it echoes back unchanged
480	            "completion_ids": [choice["token_ids"] for choice in choices],
481	            "logprobs": logprobs,
482	            "logprob_token_ids": logprob_token_ids,
483	        }

550	    def generate(
551	        self,
552	        prompts: list[list[int]],
553	        images: list[list | None] | None,
554	        num_generations: int,
555	        profiler: ProfilingContext | None = None,
556	    ) -> tuple:
557	        """Generate completions using vLLM.
558	
559	        Args:
560	            prompts: List of token ID lists, one per prompt (already tokenized).
561	            images: Optional list of image lists for VLM support. Each element is a list of PIL images for the
562	                corresponding prompt, or `None` if no images for that prompt. `None` if no images at all.
563	            num_generations: Number of generations per prompt.
564	            profiler: Optional profiler for performance tracking.
565	
566	        Returns:
567	            Tuple of (prompt_ids, completion_ids, logprobs, logprob_token_ids).
568	
569	            - `prompt_ids`: `list[list[int]]` of shape `(batch_size, prompt_len)`.
570	            - `completion_ids`: `list[list[int]]` of shape `(batch_size, completion_len)`.
571	            - `logprobs`: `list[list[list[float | None]]]` of shape `(batch_size, completion_len, num_logprobs)`.
572	            - `logprob_token_ids`: `list[list[list[int]]]` of shape `(batch_size, completion_len, num_logprobs)`.
573	
574	            `num_logprobs` is 1 when `logprobs=0`, or up to N+1 when `logprobs=N` (the sampled token is always included
575	            and may fall outside the top-N).
576	        """
577	        profiler = profiler or nullcontext()
578	        accelerator = self.accelerator
579	        temperature = self.temperature
580	        top_p = self.top_p
581	        top_k = self.top_k
582	        min_p = self.min_p
583	        repetition_penalty = self.repetition_penalty
584	        max_completion_length = self.max_completion_length
585	
586	        # Sleep level 2 discards the weights, so waking up isn't enough: they must be re-pushed from the training
587	        # model. vLLM's `reload_weights` can't be used here, as it reloads the initial checkpoint from disk rather
588	        # than the current training weights. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/29341
589	        if self.mode == "colocate" and self.enable_sleep_mode and self._llm_weights_sleeping:
590	            self.sync_weights()
591	
592	        # Generate completions using vLLM: gather all prompts and use them in a single call in the main process
593	        if self.mode == "server":
594	            all_prompts = gather_object(prompts)
595	            # Always gather images (even when None) to avoid deadlock: images may be None on some ranks
596	            # and non-None on others in mixed datasets, and gather_object is a collective operation.
597	            all_images = gather_object(images if images is not None else [None] * len(prompts))
598	            if all(img is None for img in all_images):
599	                all_images = None
600	
601	            if accelerator.is_main_process:
602	                # Since 'prompts' contains 'num_generations' duplicates, we first take unique prompts, and
603	                # generate num_generations outputs for each one. This is faster than generating outputs for each
604	                # duplicate prompt individually.
605	                ordered_set_of_prompt_ids = all_prompts[::num_generations]
606	
607	                # The server generates from either token IDs or images, so images are processed on their own first
608	                # and the resulting features are paired with the token IDs.
609	                features = None
610	                if all_images is not None:
611	                    features = self.vllm_client.image_features(all_images[::num_generations])
612	                    features = [
613	                        self._place_features(prompt_features, prompt_ids)
614	                        for prompt_features, prompt_ids in zip(features, ordered_set_of_prompt_ids, strict=True)
615	                    ]
616	
617	                sampling_params = {
618	                    "n": num_generations,
619	                    "repetition_penalty": repetition_penalty,
620	                    "temperature": temperature,
621	                    "top_p": top_p,
622	                    "top_k": top_k,
623	                    "min_p": 0.0 if min_p is None else min_p,
624	                    "max_tokens": max_completion_length,
625	                    "logprobs": self.logprobs,
626	                    "structured_outputs_regex": self.structured_outputs_regex,
627	                    "generation_kwargs": self.generation_kwargs,
628	                }
629	                with profiler:
630	                    output = self.vllm_client.generate(
631	                        prompts=ordered_set_of_prompt_ids, features=features, **sampling_params
632	                    )
633	                    payload = (
634	                        output["prompt_ids"],
635	                        output["completion_ids"],
636	                        output["logprobs"],
637	                        output.get("logprob_token_ids"),

640	                payload = None
